label: Pizzicato Strings, sampled, close and dry
audition_title: libsonare pizzicato strings vs the sampled reference
_notes: Every sixth semitone from 48 to 84, matching the tremolo strings captured from the slot beside it so the two ways of sounding one section can be read against each other. The compass is where this voice changes most, and it changes in length rather than in colour: the note falls 40 dB in 387 ms at note 48 and in 187 ms at note 84, which is the shortening a real plucked string does toward the top.
_velocities: Five, matching the slots of this rack captured earlier so that one axis covers the whole of it. The axis is live on all four of these, at 15.5 to 31.7 dB between velocity 16 and 100, so none needed the exclusion a flat velocity response would have forced.
_dry: Nothing to switch off, measured rather than assumed: with the rack loaded not one of the plugin's 1526 advertised parameters matches `reverb` or `delay`, so `dry` has no section to act on and is left off rather than claiming an effect was disabled. What the recording contains is answered by `room`, which is a different question.
_room: No room, and the answer has to be declared because no note-tail measurement can reach it: a release and a small hall are the same falling signal over the tail a capture records, and the per-note agreement test that separates a room from one note's decay passes on a release perfectly. Three independent readings say there is none here. `calibrate` measures RT60 0.00 s; with the rack loaded not one of the 1526 parameters the plugin advertises matches `reverb`, `delay` or `room`; and the pizzicato at slot 14 settles it on its own -- it reaches digital silence 450 ms after the string is plucked, inside a four-second gate, which no space permits.
_stimulus: One second, sized to the note rather than to a phrase. The longest cell of the grid is over in under half of it, so the gate holds the whole free decay with the same clearance at every note, and what the tail records is silence and the fact that there is silence.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate` on this rack, which its already-captured siblings were recorded against and whose settings this capture adopts so the slots of one rack stay comparable: a two-second settle against a measured minimum of 250 ms, and real time kept on although the reference renders the same either way, because a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement. What the recipe reports as non-determinism is worth stating precisely, because it is not round robin and a capture that recorded it as one would put a floor under the loss for nothing: two renders of the same cell correlate at 1.00000000 and peak within a thousandth of a decibel, differing only at -89 to -91 dB relative to the signal. That is one take rendered twice, not a second sample. The check is bit-identity, which is stricter than the question being asked.
_timbres: One, and the ladder is monotone above it, so this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage. That is a property of the source rather than of the work: the rack holds one slot per GM program, so there is no second pizzicato strings in it to disagree with, and `source_for` takes every timbre of a capture from one plugin, so a soundfont render cannot stand in as a second. What the reference does buy is the thing there was none of before -- a measured target for `autofit` and `--diagnose`, in place of voicing this program by ear. A second timbre needs a rack authored with an alternative in it, and this capture is written so that adding one is an edit to this list rather than a re-capture.
_dimensions: 11 of the 13 a plucked string can be judged on. `decay` is the one that matters here and it is the one the compass moves: a pizzicato is almost entirely how fast it stops, and this voice stops twice as fast at the top of the grid as at the bottom.
_dimensions_na: The exclusions as data, since a dimension argued only in prose reads as a gap.

dimensions_na.stereo: the slot renders dual mono: the two channels are bit-identical sample for sample, so the width is zero by construction rather than by voicing
dimensions_na.damper: note-off cannot be observed on this voice: the note has reached silence by 450 ms inside a 1.0 s gate, so the render is already quiet when the damper would act and there is nothing left for it to act on. The gate is left long enough to hold the whole free decay rather than shortened to make the release visible, because the decay is the measurement and the release would only be the gate's own edge

_identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `pizzicato_strings.local.json`: the plugin's component triple and the slot's preset. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/pizzicato_strings.json` and need nothing.
_slots: Slot identity is measured, never taken from a name or a position, and on this rack it is checkable against the repository's own committed measurements rather than argued from a spectrum: nine of its sixteen slots were captured in an earlier round. Rendered under each of those captures' own gates at a cell its profile holds, slot 6 returns a peak of -13.19 dBFS against a committed -13.19, slot 12 returns -16.52 against -16.52 and slot 15 returns -14.78 against -14.78. Three exact agreements fix slot n as GM program 31+n with nothing left to interpret. This slot: the one slot on the rack that is plucked and stops within half a second. Its note reaches digital silence 450 ms after the string is sounded, where the harp on the very next slot is still ringing 16 dB under its peak at 1.2 seconds and every bass on the rack is still sounding at four. Short, plucked and pitched, beside a bowed slot of the same section, is what GM 046 asks for.
